title: How a blockchain really works, and where it fails

say: How a blockchain really works, and where it fails.
This is the video for module 1 of Blockchain and Digital Assets Literacy.
A ledger is simply a record of who owns what and who paid whom. Your ajo or esusu treasurer keeps one in a notebook.

say: Step 4. The block stores the hash of the block before it. A hash is a short code, like a fingerprint for data. Change one letter, and the hash changes completely.
Because each block carries the fingerprint of the one before, the blocks form a chain.

say: Step 5. Every copy is updated. The rule that decides which block is accepted is called consensus. It replaces the trusted treasurer.

say: But remember. A blockchain only proves a record was not changed. If false information goes in, it keeps that false record forever.

say: For example, five traders led by Amaka each keep a copy of a chained record of their weekly contributions.

panel.heading: How the chain exposes cheating
items: Block 1: Amaka and Bola pay 5,000 each
Block 2 stores Block 1's fingerprint
Bola edits his copy to 50,000
His fingerprint changes; the chain breaks
4 honest copies outvote 1 altered copy

say: With a bank, one company keeps the record. A payment can often be reversed through a dispute, and customer care fixes mistakes.

panel.heading: Bank ledger and public blockchain
left: Linked to your BVN and name

say: On a public blockchain, confirmed payments are final. Nobody fixes a mistake. A wrong address usually means the money is lost.
And it is pseudonymous, not anonymous. Once an address is linked to you, your whole history can be read.

panel.heading: Bank ledger and public blockchain
left: Linked to your BVN and name

say: Bitcoin uses proof of work. Computers called miners compete to solve a hash puzzle, using a lot of electricity. A new block comes roughly every 10 minutes, and supply is capped at 21 million bitcoin.

panel.heading: Proof of work and proof of stake

say: Ethereum has used proof of stake since September 2022. Validators lock up their own ether as a deposit, and lose part of it if they cheat.
Ethereum also runs smart contracts: code that runs exactly as written, mistakes included.

panel.heading: Proof of work and proof of stake

say: Treating all crypto as one thing is the most common mistake. First, ask which category it is.

say: Before you act, know three honest limits. First, payments are final. A mistake or a scam payment usually cannot be undone.

panel.heading: Three honest limits

cards.d: No customer care can reverse a mistake or a scam payment.
A blockchain keeps false data as faithfully as true data.
Check current CBN and SEC Nigeria announcements before you act.

say: Second, a land record or delivery record on a blockchain is only as true as the person typing the data.

panel.heading: Three honest limits

cards.d: No customer care can reverse a mistake or a scam payment.
A blockchain keeps false data as faithfully as true data.
Check current CBN and SEC Nigeria announcements before you act.

say: Third, the rules in Nigeria keep changing. The Investments and Securities Act 2025 now treats digital assets as securities under SEC Nigeria.
Always check the CBN and SEC Nigeria websites before acting.

say: To remember. A blockchain is a shared ledger with no single keeper. Each block stores the fingerprint of the one before, so edits show. But tamper-evident does not mean true. Payments are final. And always name the category before you judge it.

panel.heading: Remember
items: A blockchain is a ledger with no single keeper
Each block stores the previous block's hash
Tamper-evident does not mean true
Confirmed payments are final
Always name the category of asset
